R1: src/manifest.cjs validates exact key sets without requiring property order, but compare() uses JSON.stringify(old) !== JSON.stringify(entry). Entries {"path":"a","type":"directory"} and {"type":"directory","path":"a"} therefore compare as changed despite identical contract fields. verify consequently returns 1 for an unchanged tree against a valid reordered manifest.

R2: src/manifest.cjs scan(root) calls fs.lstatSync(root) directly. On POSIX, a trailing slash requires directory resolution, so alias/ resolves a directory symlink before the root check; visit(root, '') then traverses its target. The acceptance test checks alias without a trailing slash only.

Inspected GOAL.md, cli.cjs, all src files, README.md, focused.cjs, acceptance.cjs, architecture/product specifications, and supplied logs. Code-unit sorting fixes the explicitly seeded defect. Loaded-manifest structural validation, deterministic creation encoding, output-parent realpath containment, and temporary-file replacement are present.
residual_risks: Findings are based on static inspection, not independently executed reproductions.
The documented stable-tree limitation excludes adversarial or precisely timed concurrent changes; metadata checks do not provide a locked snapshot.
